coverage_note: 10:00-14:02 Medi on a work phone call (English); 19:58-23:14 disconnect gap; 50:00-1:00:00 awal/oola/tani/nafs lesson mostly in Latin transliteration and English meta-talk; 04:14 'air conditioning' not on sheet (skipped); 04:02 شوك for شوب treated as S4; 03:06 صباح unclear, skipped; 1:01:44 غير ال شيء is a question, skipped.

rows.medi_said: لسه الـ divine يروحوا.
rows.amal_said: شو يعني لسه الزباين يروحوا؟ ... لا، لا الزباين يروحوا. There are other words, but the one we know is لا.
rows.why: He used لسه (still/yet) for 'until'; Amal questioned it and supplied la- ('la yrou7u el-zbayen'); engine wrote divine for زباين.

rows.medi_said: الساعة، uh، واح-واحد.
rows.amal_said: واحد. ... هيك الساعة واحدة.
rows.why: Clock time takes the feminine number; Amal echoed واحد back, he fixed it ('times are واحدة') and she confirmed الساعة واحدة.

rows.medi_said: اليوم بلبس بلوزة، uh، أخ-أخ-أخضر أو،
rows.amal_said: بلوزة شو؟
rows.why: بلوزة is feminine so the colour is خضرا; Amal prompted 'بلوزة شو؟' and he fixed it ('خضرا it's feminine') - he had started to self-correct with 'أو'.
rows.english: Today I'm wearing a green blouse.

rows.medi_said: Uh, uh, حافظ، حافظ. ... لا، أنا نسيت، نسيت، نسيت.
rows.amal_said: Hafiz is a motivation، بس what's about motivated؟ ... متشـ... متشجع.
rows.why: She asked for 'motivated' (the word from yesterday); he had forgotten it and she supplied متشجع.

rows.medi_said: مشجع. مشجع. ... أنا، أنا مشجع الدرس.
rows.amal_said: بس متشجع إله أو لا؟ ... هاي، هاي، برا، برا.
rows.why: He repeated her متشجع as مشجع (supporter/fan, a different form of the root) and used it again at 07:36; she kept saying متشجع but never named his form.

rows.medi_said: Is there a verb for حساب? Do you guys use it?
rows.amal_said: بحسب.
rows.why: He asked for the verb 'to consider'; Amal supplied بحسب.

rows.medi_said: أنا، أنا مشجع الدرس.
rows.why: Amal's own questions used متشجع إله / للـ شغل - the adjective takes la-; he dropped it (my reading).

rows.medi_said: أنا في الـ Wi-Fi? Is that how you say it?
rows.amal_said: Yeah I'm on the wifi أنا عالـ wifi.
rows.why: 'On the wifi' takes 3ala, not fi; Amal recast أنا عالـ wifi.

rows.medi_said: أنا على Wi-Fi?
rows.amal_said: على الـ، عالـ.
rows.why: He dropped the el- after على; Amal repeated على الـ / عالـ.

rows.medi_said: So Shanteti, ... Would it be El Shogol? ... El Shogolelah El, uh, Amra.
rows.amal_said: Yes, but what's work bag without any my or yours?
rows.why: The possessive goes on the last noun of the idafa and the first word takes no el-/ending; Amal prompted and he fixed it ('Shantet Shogoli, not Shanteti Shogoli').

rows.medi_said: So Shantet Shogoli, uh, uh, Amra.
rows.amal_said: That would mean is red. ... if it's possessed by a pronoun it's definitive, so the adjective after it should be definitive as well.
rows.why: A possessed noun is definite so its adjective needs el-; without it the phrase becomes a sentence 'is red' - Amal named the rule.

rows.medi_said: So would it be شنتت، شنتت شغلي الأحمر، الأحمر،
rows.amal_said: الحمرا.
rows.why: شنتة is feminine so the adjective is الحمرا; Amal recast it.

rows.medi_said: شنتت شغلي، اه، الحمراء، اه، ما فيهون.
rows.amal_said: ما فيهن means there aren't here or there isn't here. ... Yeah, مشون.
rows.why: 'Not here' is mish hon (mish before a non-verb); ma fi means 'there isn't' - Amal explained and confirmed مش هون.
rows.english: My red work bag is not here.

rows.medi_said: اسم. اسمى. اسميت.
rows.amal_said: ليش؟ لا، ليش. ... It's just اسم. Why would it be feminine?
rows.why: He added the feminine -t to اسم (a masculine noun) in idafa; Amal said no, it's just اسم.

rows.medi_said: uh, الـ، الـ اسم،
rows.amal_said: لا.
rows.why: The first word of an idafa never takes el-; Amal said لا (and again at 30:21).
rows.english: the old name of his school

rows.medi_said: So الـ اسم قديم. No, it's like اسم القديمة.
rows.amal_said: لا. لا. You just change the gender of Adeem.
rows.why: To mean 'the old name' the adjective must match اسم (masculine): el-2adeem; Amal said no and told him to change the gender of 2adeem.
rows.english: the old name of his school

rows.medi_said: محل الأواى المفضل.
rows.amal_said: But her. Her favorite store. Her store favorite.
rows.why: He left out 'her'; Amal prompted 'But her' and he put -ha on the last noun (36:38, 37:16 محل أواعيها المفضل).

rows.medi_said: So أحسن المحل.
rows.amal_said: No. Even though in English we don't-- we say the, in Arabic we don't.
rows.why: A superlative before the noun takes no el-; Amal said No and named the rule.

rows.medi_said: هذي المحل أحسن إشي.
rows.amal_said: Mm, it works, yeah. هذا أحسن محل is like more efficient.
rows.why: محل is masculine so it is هذا (my reading); she accepted the structure and modelled هذا أحسن محل without naming the gender.

rows.medi_said: آل الزبون. No, not-- أس-- أسوأ الزبون. ... أسوأ الزبون.
rows.amal_said: The worst.
rows.why: Superlative + noun takes no el- (just taught at 41:23); he said أسوأ الزبون twice and she only typed aswa2 zboon (chat alone is not a voiced fix).

rows.medi_said: Okay. So أحسن الزبون ما، ما تشتري إشي.
rows.why: He was building 'the worst customer is the one who doesn't buy' but said أحسن (best); her chat keeps aswa2 (my reading).
rows.english: The worst customer doesn't buy anything.

rows.medi_said: ما، ما تشتري إشي. ما بتشتري. ما بتشتري.
rows.amal_said: It's ما بي، ما بيشتري because it's زبون.
rows.why: زبون is masculine so the verb is the he-form بيشتري; Amal recast and gave the reason.

rows.medi_said: الناس. Okay. اللي، اللي بحب أكتر إشي.
rows.amal_said: No, no. First you have to say the one... Oh, okay. Yes, it actually works. إلي.
rows.why: After illi the verb needs the pointer ending -o; after Amal's 'no, no' he rebuilt it as اللي بحبه أكتر إشي (45:37), matching her chat.
rows.english: the one I like the most

rows.medi_said: أكتر هذا إشي? ... أكتر هذا. ... أكتر هذا بحبه.
rows.amal_said: أكثر حدا بحبه. ... أكثر حدا.
rows.why: He used هذا (this) for حدا (someone) three times; Amal recast أكثر حدا each time. Sheet: 'someone | 7ada | حدا'.
rows.english: the person I like the most

rows.medi_said: هذا. أكتر هذا بحب.
rows.amal_said: بحبه.
rows.why: The verb needs the pointer -o back to the person; Amal recast بحبه and he said 'There's a pointer'.
rows.english: the person I like the most

rows.medi_said: The week's beginning.
rows.amal_said: Why? ... if you say the week's beginning, now you'd have to be إضافة ... أول has to be before أسبوع.
rows.why: He read her الأسبوع الأول (noun + adjective) as 'the week's beginning'; Amal asked why and explained it means the first week.

rows.medi_said: Il awal il tamreen or il tamreen il awal is the first exercise.
rows.amal_said: Mm-hmm. ... Of course.
rows.why: Amal had just taught that أول before a noun never takes el- (48:15, 49:30); he put el- on it and she let it pass.
rows.proposed_rule: أول / آخر / تاني before the noun never take el- (awal sayyaara); after the noun they are adjectives and take el- (el-laffe el-oola)

rows.medi_said: Laffe ul-- Laffe il aula? ... Laffe aula.
rows.amal_said: Al laffa al oola. ... Al laffa, what does al laffa mean?
rows.chat: awal laffe, awal el-lafe, el-laffe el-oola
rows.why: He could not parse her el-laffe el-oola (noun + adjective, el- on both); she repeated it and walked him to 'the first drive'.

rows.medi_said: Uh, something else. ... Something else?
rows.amal_said: Tani ishi. ... The second thing.
rows.why: He glossed تاني إشي as 'something else'; Amal corrected: it is 'the second thing', إشي تاني is 'something else' (sheet: 'something else | Eshi taani').

rows.medi_said: So nafs ishi.
rows.amal_said: Nafs al ishi. ... نفس إشي doesn't mean anything.
rows.why: Amal recast نفس الـ إشي and said نفس إشي means nothing.
rows.proposed_rule: نفس (same) is followed by the noun WITH el-: nafs el-ishi = the same thing; nafs ishi is wrong
